summary: Helena-Lewis and Clark NF lookout north of Lincoln, MT; build date disputed (1941-1950 sources); current frame cab from mid-1990s; staffed in summer; standing; 4x4 road open July-October.

facts.design: L-4 tower in 1945 (firelookout.com); current frame cabin on a 10-ft concrete base, built mid-1990s

access.note: Unpaved road about 18 miles from Lincoln; a 4x4 is required; open July through October and closed in winter (DangerousRoads). The cab is an active staffed lookout.

visit.trail_note: Road is totally unpaved, rocky and steep in spots; the cab is staffed in summer. The advice not to climb it is editorial, not from a source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A March 1941 newspaper item, firelookout.com's 1945 date, and a 1965 recovery note describing a tower built in 1950 disagree. Not resolved; the story says so.
KRTV gives 8,270 ft, which matches the brief's 2,520.7 m. DangerousRoads gives 8,284 ft (2,525 m). Not resolved.
firelookout.com says the tower was torn down soon after staffing ended in 1963. The 1965 recovery note says it was reported removed in 1964. The difference is one year.
KRTV describes a wood and cinder block tower. firelookout.com describes a frame cabin on a 10-ft concrete base. These may describe the same building; not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Build date is disputed: 1941 newspaper (CCC-era lookout house and tower), 1945 per firelookout.com and DangerousRoads, 1950 tower per a 1965 recovery note. The story presents all three. The KRTV feature is undated in the cached copy, so the staffing as_of is only as current as that article. The brief's height_m of 3.0 looks like the 10-ft base and was not used. The brief's 2009 restored event was corrected to repairs. Access is public for the road; the cab is an active lookout and the story advises against climbing. Newspaper items are cited through Rex's page, not the original papers. I did not check NHLR or a Forest Service page for Stonewall. The 1964 quote is split across a line break in the source, so it is quoted separately.
